E-APP-001.user_message: No connection. Reconnect to continue. Your last tap was not saved.
E-APP-001.what_happened: The performer app tried to send a tap (or load today's list) while the device had no connection, or the request failed at the network level before reaching the server.
E-APP-001.likely_cause: The phone or computer lost its connection.
E-APP-001.fix_hint: Reconnect and tap again. Nothing was queued on purpose — the MVP has no offline mode, so a queued tap could silently go stale.

E-APP-002.user_message: That didn't save. Tap again. Reference: {ref}.
E-APP-002.what_happened: A tap reached the server (or the request otherwise failed) but did not come back with a clear answer — a 500, a timeout, or a response the app could not parse.
E-APP-002.likely_cause: A transient server problem, or a bug in the endpoint being called.
E-APP-002.fix_hint: Tapping again is safe — the log row and the task's status are written together, so a failed attempt leaves neither, and a repeat with the same client_event_id is a no-op if the first one actually landed. If this repeats, check the Health page for a matching failure event.

E-APP-003.what_happened: A performer tried to act on a step that isn't scheduled to them, or asked for a step id that doesn't belong to their account.
E-APP-003.likely_cause: The step was reassigned, the link was stale, or the id belongs to someone else's work.
E-APP-003.fix_hint: Reload today's list. If the step really should be theirs, check the assignment in the plan.

E-APP-004.what_happened: The stored session token was missing, expired, or rejected by the server.
E-APP-004.likely_cause: The session expired, or the token was revoked.
E-APP-004.fix_hint: Sign in again. Nothing from before the expiry was lost — every tap up to that point was already recorded.

E-APP-005.user_message: Something went wrong. Reference: {ref}. We've recorded it.
E-APP-005.what_happened: An error the app did not anticipate — an unhandled exception in the performer screen, or a response shape it didn't expect.
E-APP-005.likely_cause: A bug, or a backend response that changed shape.
E-APP-005.fix_hint: Quote the Reference on the Health page to find the exact event. The screen recovers to a safe empty state rather than staying crashed.

E-DEL-001.user_message: Something is using this map, so it can’t be deleted.
E-DEL-001.what_happened: A journey map was deleted while a plan, a template or a job still depended on it.
E-DEL-001.likely_cause: The map was attached to a plan or template earlier, or work was already created from it.
E-DEL-001.fix_hint: The message names what is using it. Remove the map there first, or leave it in place — an unused map can always be deleted later. Deleting it anyway would leave that plan pointing at a map that no longer exists.
E-DEL-001.message_varies_why: The sentence names the plan or template that is using the map.

E-DEL-002.user_message: Only the person who created this map, or an account admin, can delete it.
E-DEL-002.what_happened: Someone tried to delete a map they do not own and is not an admin for.
E-DEL-002.likely_cause: Maps belonging to the whole account became visible to everyone on 2026-10-17, so a teammate’s map now appears in your list.
E-DEL-002.fix_hint: Ask the person who created it, or an account admin. You can still open and read the map — only deleting it is restricted.

E-GOV-001.user_message: You don't have access to this.
E-GOV-001.what_happened: Someone tried to read or change something that belongs to a different account.
E-GOV-001.likely_cause: A stale link or bookmark pointing at another account's data, or a bug passing the wrong id.
E-GOV-001.fix_hint: Check the Health page timeline for this Reference to see which entity and account were involved. If it keeps happening for a real user, a screen is probably loading an id it shouldn't have.

E-GOV-002.user_message: Those two things belong to different accounts, so they can't be linked.
E-GOV-002.what_happened: An action tried to connect two records that live in different accounts.
E-GOV-002.likely_cause: A picker or form offered an option from outside the current account.
E-GOV-002.fix_hint: Find the two entity ids on the Health page timeline for this Reference, then check which screen offered the cross-account option.

E-GOV-003.user_message: This can't be done while it's in its current state.
E-GOV-003.what_happened: An action was attempted on something whose status doesn't allow it, for example editing a plan that is already live.
E-GOV-003.likely_cause: The screen was showing an out-of-date status, usually because it hadn't been reloaded.
E-GOV-003.fix_hint: Reload the page to see the current status. If the status looks right and the action still fails, check the Health page for the expected states.

E-GOV-004.user_message: This has been archived, so it can't be changed.
E-GOV-004.what_happened: A write was attempted against an archived record.
E-GOV-004.likely_cause: The item was archived in another tab or by someone else since this screen was opened.
E-GOV-004.fix_hint: Reload to confirm it is archived. Archived items are kept for history on purpose and are never edited again.

E-GOV-005.user_message: Someone else changed this. Reload to see the latest.
E-GOV-005.what_happened: Two people edited the same record, and the second save was refused so it couldn't overwrite the first.
E-GOV-005.likely_cause: Two tabs or two people working on the same plan at the same time.
E-GOV-005.fix_hint: Reload and redo the change. Nothing was lost: the refused save was never written.

E-GOV-006.user_message: The daily data check found records pointing at things that no longer exist.
E-GOV-006.what_happened: The integrity audit found rows whose parent record has been deleted — for example journey cells still pointing at a map that is gone — or a stage whose owner key matches no row in its map.
E-GOV-006.likely_cause: Something was deleted without cleaning up what pointed at it. The database does not enforce this on its own, which is why the audit exists.
E-GOV-006.fix_hint: Open the Health page and copy the diagnostic bundle. The counts show which check failed and how often. Orphans are safe to leave in place short-term (nothing reads them), but the delete path that created them needs a guard so it stops happening.

E-JOB-001.user_message: Give the job a short title (up to 120 characters).
E-JOB-001.what_happened: A job was added with no title, a title over 120 characters, or one containing HTML tags.
E-JOB-001.likely_cause: The title box was left empty, or text was pasted in from a web page and brought formatting with it.
E-JOB-001.fix_hint: A job title is how people recognise this piece of work in a list — a customer name or a reference is usually enough. Paste as plain text if you copied it from elsewhere. Your typing was kept.

E-JOB-002.user_message: This plan doesn't use that map. Add it to the plan's maps first.
E-JOB-002.what_happened: A job was added for a journey map the plan does not accept.
E-JOB-002.likely_cause: The plan was created from a template that did not include this map, or the map was added to the template after this plan was made.
E-JOB-002.fix_hint: The full message names the map. A plan's accepted maps are copied from its template when the plan is created, so adding a map to the template later does not reach plans that already exist — add it to this plan directly.

E-JOB-003.user_message: That map hasn't been published yet.
E-JOB-003.what_happened: A job was added for a map that has never had a version published.
E-JOB-003.likely_cause: The map is still a draft.
E-JOB-003.fix_hint: Open the map and publish a version. A job pins itself to the published version it was created from, so there has to be one before any work can be based on it.

E-JOB-004.user_message: That detail isn't valid. Use short text or a number.
E-JOB-004.what_happened: A job detail was rejected: the name used characters other than letters, numbers and underscores, the value was over 200 characters, or the job already has 50 details.
E-JOB-004.likely_cause: A space or punctuation in the detail's name, or a long note pasted into a value.
E-JOB-004.fix_hint: Detail names look like customer_name or order_ref. Long explanations belong in the job's own notes rather than in a detail. Replacing a detail the job already has always works, even at the 50 limit.

E-JOB-005.what_happened: Cancel was called on a job that had already been cancelled.
E-JOB-005.likely_cause: The button was clicked twice, or a request was retried.
E-JOB-005.fix_hint: Nothing went wrong and nothing changed — cancelling twice is harmless. The job's tasks are left exactly as they were, because a cancelled job is still history.

E-LIVE-001.user_message: There's nothing on this timeline to publish.
E-LIVE-001.what_happened: Publish to live was attempted on a day with no work scheduled on it.
E-LIVE-001.likely_cause: The day was created but nothing has been dragged onto it yet.
E-LIVE-001.fix_hint: Schedule at least one piece of work on the day first. Publishing an empty day would show the person an empty list.

E-LIVE-002.user_message: Some steps don't have a person assigned.
E-LIVE-002.what_happened: Publish to live was refused because at least one scheduled step has nobody to do it.
E-LIVE-002.likely_cause: A step was scheduled onto a day without picking who does it, and the day has no default person either.
E-LIVE-002.fix_hint: The full message says how many. Assign someone to each step, or set the day's person. Nothing was published.

E-LIVE-003.user_message: Some steps are marked 'needs info'. Complete them first.
E-LIVE-003.what_happened: Publish to live was refused because at least one step is still waiting on information.
E-LIVE-003.likely_cause: Someone flagged a step as needing information and it has not been resolved.
E-LIVE-003.fix_hint: Open each flagged step, deal with what it is waiting on, and set it back to planned. Sending someone work that is known to be incomplete wastes their time.

E-LIVE-004.user_message: That person doesn't have a login yet, so they can't see their work.
E-LIVE-004.what_happened: Publish to live was refused because an assigned person has no linked login.
E-LIVE-004.likely_cause: The person was added to the plan as a name, without being connected to a user account.
E-LIVE-004.fix_hint: The full message names them. Link their login on the agent, or assign the work to someone who has one. Publishing to a person who cannot sign in would look successful and deliver nothing.

E-LIVE-005.what_happened: Publish to live was attempted on a day that has already been published.
E-LIVE-005.likely_cause: The button was clicked twice, or the day was published from another screen.
E-LIVE-005.fix_hint: Nothing changed. A day is published once — the frozen copy the person sees must not move under them. Later planner changes are recorded separately and stay with the planner.

E-LIVE-006.user_message: We couldn't publish. Nothing was changed.
E-LIVE-006.what_happened: Publishing failed partway and was rolled back.
E-LIVE-006.likely_cause: A database or connection problem during the write.
E-LIVE-006.fix_hint: Try again. The publication and the day's status are written together, so a failure leaves no half-published day. If it keeps happening, copy the diagnostic bundle from the Health page.

E-LIVE-007.user_message: This person has already started this day — it can no longer be republished.
E-LIVE-007.what_happened: Republish was refused because the performer has already recorded work against this day's published plan.
E-LIVE-007.likely_cause: Work began between opening the planner and clicking republish, or the day was simply already underway.
E-LIVE-007.fix_hint: The full message names who. The day is sealed on purpose: what someone is measured against must not change once they have begun. Later planner edits are still allowed and logged — they just never reach the performer's frozen view.

E-LIVE-008.user_message: This day was just published by someone else — reload and try again.
E-LIVE-008.what_happened: Two publishes of the same day overlapped; this one lost the race and wrote nothing.
E-LIVE-008.likely_cause: Two planner windows, or two people, published the same timeline at the same moment.
E-LIVE-008.fix_hint: Reload to see the version that won. If your changes are still missing, make them again and publish — nothing from the losing attempt was saved.

E-LOG-001.user_message: That action isn't available for this step right now.
E-LOG-001.what_happened: An action was taken that isn't allowed from the step's current state — for example starting something already finished.
E-LOG-001.likely_cause: The screen was showing an out-of-date state, or someone else moved the step first.
E-LOG-001.fix_hint: The full message says what state the step is in and what to do instead — usually reopening it, or unblocking it first. Nothing was recorded.

E-LOG-002.user_message: Pick a reason so the team knows why.
E-LOG-002.what_happened: A step was marked blocked without choosing a reason.
E-LOG-002.fix_hint: Choose one of the four reasons. A blocked step with no reason tells the planner there is a problem but nothing about what to chase, which is barely better than not flagging it.

E-LOG-003.user_message: This step isn't assigned to you.
E-LOG-003.what_happened: Someone tried to record progress on work that belongs to another person.
E-LOG-003.likely_cause: A stale link, or the work was reassigned after the screen loaded.
E-LOG-003.fix_hint: Refresh your list. If the work really is yours, ask the planner to reassign it to you — the record needs to show who actually did it.

E-LOG-004.user_message: Your tap wasn't saved. Please try again.
E-LOG-004.what_happened: Recording an action failed and was rolled back.
E-LOG-004.likely_cause: A connection or database problem at the moment of the tap.
E-LOG-004.fix_hint: Tap again — repeats are safe, because the same tap is never recorded twice. The log entry and the step's status are written together, so a failure leaves neither. This is the most important write path in the product; repeated failures should be looked at immediately.

E-LOG-005.user_message: Pick one of the listed reasons.
E-LOG-005.what_happened: A blocked step was sent with a reason that isn't one of the four allowed.
E-LOG-005.likely_cause: A client sent its own wording instead of choosing from the list.
E-LOG-005.fix_hint: The reasons are a fixed list so they can be counted and compared across jobs. Free text belongs in the note instead.

E-LOG-006.what_happened: A note was saved with no text.
E-LOG-006.likely_cause: The note box was submitted empty.
E-LOG-006.fix_hint: An empty note was always accepted before APP-2 (US-APP-2-02) added this check — the Step screen's own box also refuses an empty save, but this is the one that actually enforces it.

E-LOG-007.user_message: Notes can be up to 1,000 characters.
E-LOG-007.what_happened: A note was longer than the allowed length.
E-LOG-007.likely_cause: Pasted text, or several notes combined into one.
E-LOG-007.fix_hint: Shorten the note and save again. The typed text is kept on screen, per CLAUDE.md's rule to never discard a rejected save's input.

E-OBS-001.user_message: You don't have access to this page.
E-OBS-001.what_happened: A non-admin user (or an unauthenticated request) tried to reach an ops/* endpoint or the Health page.
E-OBS-001.likely_cause: The caller's user record does not have is_platform_admin set to true.
E-OBS-001.fix_hint: If this user should be a platform admin, set user.is_platform_admin = true directly in the database. There is no UI for this on purpose.

E-OBS-002.user_message: Too many reports were sent in a short time, so we slowed down.
E-OBS-002.what_happened: The client event endpoint's rate limit (20 per minute per user) was hit, usually from a screen stuck in an error loop.
E-OBS-002.likely_cause: A front-end bug is repeatedly failing and reporting the same error.
E-OBS-002.fix_hint: Check the Health page's issue list for the feature/step that is flooding, and fix the underlying front-end error.

E-P3A-001.user_message: This plan has work recorded against it. Archive it instead.
E-P3A-001.what_happened: A delete was refused because the plan already has jobs, a publication or logged activity.
E-P3A-001.likely_cause: Someone tried to delete a plan that has already been used, rather than archiving it.
E-P3A-001.fix_hint: Archive the plan. It disappears from the plan list and stops accepting changes, but everything already recorded against it stays intact. Deleting is only possible for a plan nothing has happened on yet.

E-P3A-002.user_message: This agent has recorded work, so they can't be removed.
E-P3A-002.what_happened: An agent with a published day or logged activity was deleted.
E-P3A-002.likely_cause: Someone tried to remove a person who has already done work.
E-P3A-002.fix_hint: Hide them from the roster instead. Their recorded work still points at them, so the row has to stay.

E-P3A-003.user_message: This timeline is live. It can't be deleted.
E-P3A-003.likely_cause: Someone tried to remove a day that has already been handed to a performer.
E-P3A-003.fix_hint: Publishing freezes a day. Its contents can still be reassigned, but the day itself stays.

E-PLAN-001.user_message: Give the template a unique name (up to 80 characters).
E-PLAN-001.what_happened: A plan template was saved with no name, a name over 80 characters, or a name another template in the same account already uses.
E-PLAN-001.likely_cause: The name was left blank, or a template for this purpose already exists.
E-PLAN-001.fix_hint: Check the template list first — if one already covers this, edit it rather than making a second. Your typing was kept.

E-PLAN-002.user_message: Choose a window between 1 and 366 days.
E-PLAN-002.what_happened: A template's planning window was saved as zero, negative, or longer than a year.
E-PLAN-002.likely_cause: The field was left at zero, or a number of weeks was typed where days were expected.
E-PLAN-002.fix_hint: The window is in days and counts both the first and last day, so a fortnight is 14, not 15.

E-PLAN-003.what_happened: A template's default start time was not a 24-hour HH:MM value.
E-PLAN-003.likely_cause: A single-digit hour ("8:00"), or an hour above 23.
E-PLAN-003.fix_hint: Use two digits for both parts. This is the time each day starts in plans made from this template; it can still be changed per day afterwards.

E-PLAN-004.user_message: Only published maps can be used in a plan.
E-PLAN-004.what_happened: A journey map was attached to a template before it had ever been published.
E-PLAN-004.likely_cause: The map is still a draft, so there is no fixed version of it for a plan to work from.
E-PLAN-004.fix_hint: Open the map and publish a version, then attach it. The full message names the map. Publishing freezes a copy, which is what stops a plan's work changing underneath it later.

E-PLAN-005.user_message: This plan has work recorded against it, so it can't be deleted. Archive it instead.
E-PLAN-005.what_happened: A delete was refused because the plan already has jobs, a publication or logged activity.
E-PLAN-005.likely_cause: Someone tried to delete a plan that has already been used.
E-PLAN-005.fix_hint: Archive the plan. It leaves the plan list and stops accepting changes, but everything recorded against it stays intact.

E-PLAN-006.user_message: This person is already set up as an agent.
E-PLAN-006.what_happened: A user was tagged as an agent a second time.
E-PLAN-006.likely_cause: They already have a profile; the create form was submitted again for the same person.
E-PLAN-006.fix_hint: Find their existing profile and edit it instead of creating a new one — one profile per real login.

E-PLAN-007.user_message: Give this AI agent a name.
E-PLAN-007.what_happened: An AI agent profile (no login) was saved with no name.
E-PLAN-007.likely_cause: The name field was left blank — a person profile gets its name from their login, but an AI profile has no login to borrow one from.
E-PLAN-007.fix_hint: Name the AI agent directly, same as naming one inside a plan today.

E-PLAN-008.user_message: Daily capacity must be a positive number of hours.
E-PLAN-008.what_happened: An agent profile's default daily capacity was zero or negative.
E-PLAN-008.likely_cause: The field was left at zero or a negative number was typed.
E-PLAN-008.fix_hint: Enter the usual number of hours this person or AI agent is expected to work in a day — it's only a default, and can still be changed per plan.

E-PLAN-009.what_happened: An agent profile's color wasn't a 6-digit hex value.
E-PLAN-009.likely_cause: A color name or a shorthand 3-digit hex was typed instead of the full 6-digit form.

E-PLAN-010.user_message: This person isn't tagged as an agent right now.
E-PLAN-010.what_happened: A template tried to add an agent profile that's currently marked ineligible.
E-PLAN-010.likely_cause: The profile was toggled off (PLAN-2) after it was last used, or was never fully set up.
E-PLAN-010.fix_hint: Re-enable the agent's profile first, or pick someone else.

E-PLAN-011.user_message: That user isn't on this account.
E-PLAN-011.what_happened: An agent profile was requested for a user outside the caller's account.
E-PLAN-011.likely_cause: A stale or mistaken user id.
E-PLAN-011.fix_hint: Only teammates on this account can be tagged as agents.

E-PLAN-012.user_message: Two agents on this template would both be called the same name. Rename one, or leave one off.
E-PLAN-012.what_happened: An agent was added to a template roster whose display name matches another agent already on it (ignoring capitals and spaces).
E-PLAN-012.likely_cause: An AI agent named like a person, or two people with the same name.
E-PLAN-012.fix_hint: A plan can't hold two agents with the same name, so every plan made from this template would fail. Rename one in the Agents screen, then add it again.

E-PLAN-013.user_message: Only an account admin can set up or change agents for other people, or AI agents.
E-PLAN-013.what_happened: A non-admin tried to tag, untag or edit someone else's agent profile, or an AI agent's.
E-PLAN-013.likely_cause: A member trying to manage the team's agent list.
E-PLAN-013.fix_hint: Members can manage their own profile only. Ask an account admin to make the change.
E-PLAN-013.message_varies_why: Same admin-only rule, worded for create vs edit.

E-PLAN-014.user_message: That template is archived, so new plans can't be made from it.
E-PLAN-014.what_happened: A plan was created from a template that has been archived.
E-PLAN-014.likely_cause: The template was archived after the screen was opened, or an old link was used.
E-PLAN-014.fix_hint: Un-archive the template, or pick a different one. Plans already made from it are unaffected.

E-PLAN-015.user_message: One of those maps isn't available to this account.
E-PLAN-015.what_happened: A map was attached that does not belong to this account.
E-PLAN-015.likely_cause: A stale list, or an id from somewhere else.
E-PLAN-015.fix_hint: Reload the picker. It only offers maps this account owns; anything else is refused server-side.

E-PLAN-016.user_message: One of those agents isn't available to this account.
E-PLAN-016.what_happened: An agent profile was added to a template but does not belong to this account.
E-PLAN-016.likely_cause: A stale list, or an id from somewhere else.
E-PLAN-016.fix_hint: Reload the Agents screen. Only this account’s agents can go on a template roster.

E-PLN-001.user_message: You already have a plan with this name.
E-PLN-001.what_happened: A plan was created or renamed to a name another plan in the same account already uses.
E-PLN-001.likely_cause: Two plans were given the same name, or the same create was submitted twice.
E-PLN-001.fix_hint: Pick a different name. Names only have to be unique within your own account, so another company using the same name is not the problem. Your typing was kept.

E-PLN-002.user_message: The end date can't be before the start date.
E-PLN-002.what_happened: A plan's planning window was saved with its end earlier than its start.
E-PLN-002.likely_cause: One of the two dates was changed without looking at the other.
E-PLN-002.fix_hint: Check both dates. Changing only one of them still has to leave the window the right way round, so the saved value for the other date is what it was compared against.

E-PLN-003.user_message: This has to be zero or more.
E-PLN-003.what_happened: A plan's AI throughput setting was saved as a negative number.
E-PLN-003.likely_cause: A minus sign was typed, or a field was pre-filled with a bad value.
E-PLN-003.fix_hint: Enter zero or a positive number. Zero means the plan makes no AI throughput assumption at all.

E-PLN-004.user_message: You already have a model with this id.
E-PLN-004.what_happened: A model was added using an id another model in the same account already uses.
E-PLN-004.likely_cause: The model was already added, or the id differs only by capitalisation — ids are lower-cased, so "GPT-X" and "gpt-x" are the same id.
E-PLN-004.fix_hint: Check the model list first. If the existing one has the wrong prices, edit it rather than adding a second.

E-PLN-005.user_message: A model's id can't be changed after it's created. Add a new model instead.
E-PLN-005.what_happened: An edit tried to change a model's id.
E-PLN-005.likely_cause: A rename was attempted on the id rather than on the display name.
E-PLN-005.fix_hint: The display name can be changed freely — change that instead. The id is fixed because "reset to defaults" uses it to recognise the built-in models. To really change an id, add a new model and point the agents at it.

E-PLN-006.user_message: This model is still used by some agents. Point them at another model first.
E-PLN-006.what_happened: A model could not be deleted because agents still reference it.
E-PLN-006.likely_cause: The model is assigned to one or more AI agents in a plan.
E-PLN-006.fix_hint: The full message names each agent using the model. Open each one and pick a different model, then delete this one. Nothing was deleted.

E-PLN-007.user_message: This plan already has someone with that name.
E-PLN-007.what_happened: An agent was added or renamed to a name another agent in the same plan already uses.
E-PLN-007.likely_cause: Two people with the same first name, or the same person added twice.
E-PLN-007.fix_hint: Use something that tells them apart, like a surname or initial. Names only have to be unique inside one plan, so the same name is fine in a different plan. Your typing was kept.

E-PLN-008.user_message: Only AI agents can have a model.
E-PLN-008.what_happened: A model was assigned to an agent whose kind is "person".
E-PLN-008.likely_cause: The kind was switched to person without clearing the model, or the wrong agent was being edited.
E-PLN-008.fix_hint: A model is only used to work out token costs, which only apply to AI agents. Either switch this agent to AI, or leave the model unset. Switching an AI agent to a person clears its model automatically.

E-PLN-009.user_message: Daily capacity has to be more than 0 and no more than 24 hours.
E-PLN-009.what_happened: An agent's daily capacity was saved outside the range a day allows.
E-PLN-009.likely_cause: A zero, a negative number, or a value above 24 was entered.
E-PLN-009.fix_hint: Enter the hours this person or agent is available on a normal day. Zero would mean they can never be scheduled, so use hide instead if that is what you want.

E-PLN-010.user_message: Enter a start time as HH:MM, between 00:00 and 23:59.
E-PLN-010.what_happened: A timeline's start time was saved in a format the planner could not read.
E-PLN-010.likely_cause: A single-digit hour or minute ("8:5"), a 24-hour value above 23, or the field left blank.
E-PLN-010.fix_hint: Use two digits for both parts, like 08:00 or 14:30. Your typing was kept.

E-PLN-011.user_message: A timeline's status is set by publishing, not here.
E-PLN-011.what_happened: A create or edit tried to set a timeline's status directly.
E-PLN-011.likely_cause: A client sent the whole timeline object back, including its status, instead of just the fields being changed.
E-PLN-011.fix_hint: Status only ever changes when a plan is published to live. Leave it out of the request. Nothing was saved.

E-PLN-012.user_message: That agent already has a timeline on that date.
E-PLN-012.what_happened: A timeline was dragged onto a day where that agent already has one.
E-PLN-012.likely_cause: The target cell looked empty, or two people were editing the schedule at once.
E-PLN-012.fix_hint: One person gets one timeline per day. Move it to a free day, or open the existing timeline and move the tasks across. Nothing was changed, and the two days were not merged.

E-PLN-013.user_message: How long should this take? Enter between 1 minute and 24 hours.
E-PLN-013.what_happened: A task's duration was saved as zero, negative, or longer than a day.
E-PLN-013.likely_cause: The field was left at zero, or a number of hours was typed where minutes were expected.
E-PLN-013.fix_hint: Durations are in minutes, so an hour and a half is 90. A task longer than a day should be split into several. Your typing was kept.

E-PLN-014.user_message: Say what's missing, so whoever picks this up knows what to chase.
E-PLN-014.what_happened: A task was flagged as needing information, with no explanation of what is needed.
E-PLN-014.likely_cause: The status was changed without filling in the reason box.
E-PLN-014.fix_hint: Write a short note about what you are waiting on. Setting the task back to planned clears the note automatically.

E-PLN-015.what_happened: A task was moved to a negative position in a list.
E-PLN-015.likely_cause: A drag-and-drop sent a bad index — this is a bug in the screen, not something typed.
E-PLN-015.fix_hint: Dropping past the end of a list is fine and lands the task at the end. A negative position means the caller computed the drop point wrongly. Nothing was moved.

E-PLN-016.user_message: That new order doesn't match this day's tasks, so nothing was changed.
E-PLN-016.what_happened: A reorder was sent that did not list exactly the tasks currently on that day — one was missing, repeated, or did not belong.
E-PLN-016.likely_cause: The day changed in another tab or by someone else while this screen was open.
E-PLN-016.fix_hint: Reload the day and drag again. The order was left exactly as it was — a partial reorder is never applied.

E-ORD-001.user_message: That column (or row) order doesn't match this map, so nothing was changed. Refresh and try again.
E-ORD-001.what_happened: A reorder of a journey map's columns or rows was sent that did not list exactly the columns/rows currently in the map — one was missing, repeated, or belonged to a different map.
E-ORD-001.likely_cause: The map changed in another tab, or someone else added or removed a column/row while this screen was open.
E-ORD-001.fix_hint: Reload the map and move it again. The order was left exactly as it was — a partial reorder is never applied. Different from E-PLN-016, which is the same rule for a planner day.

E-ORD-002.user_message: The column (or row) you tried to insert next to isn't in this map any more, so nothing was added. Refresh and try again.
E-ORD-002.what_happened: An insert-at-position named an after_stage_id / after_lens_id that is not a column/row of this map.
E-ORD-002.likely_cause: The screen is stale: that column or row was removed (or moved to another map) after the page loaded. Refetch, don't retry.
E-ORD-002.fix_hint: Reload the map; the seam + will then point at real columns/rows. Nothing was created.

E-PLN-017.user_message: That login doesn't belong to this account.
E-PLN-017.what_happened: An agent was linked to a login from a different account.
E-PLN-017.likely_cause: The person was removed from the account after the screen was opened.
E-PLN-017.fix_hint: Pick someone from this account’s own list. An agent can only be performed by a login that belongs here.

E-PLN-018.user_message: That login is already linked to someone else in this plan.
E-PLN-018.what_happened: Two agents in one plan were pointed at the same login.
E-PLN-018.likely_cause: The same person added twice under different names.
E-PLN-018.fix_hint: One login, one agent, per plan — otherwise their day would arrive twice. Unlink the other agent first.

E-PUB-001.user_message: This map isn't ready yet. Open the checklist to see what needs attention.
E-PUB-001.what_happened: Publish was refused because the map did not pass the readiness gate.
E-PUB-001.likely_cause: Something on the checklist is still missing: a title, a stage owner, a task, or an expected duration.
E-PUB-001.fix_hint: Open the checklist on the map. Every unticked item is a thing to fill in. Nothing was published and nothing was lost.

E-PUB-003.user_message: This saved version doesn't match its own record. Someone should look into it.
E-PUB-003.what_happened: A published version's stored content no longer matches the fingerprint taken when it was published.
E-PUB-003.likely_cause: The row was changed outside the publish path: a direct database edit, a restore gone wrong, or tampering.
E-PUB-003.fix_hint: Do not edit the row. Copy the diagnostic bundle from the Health page. Published versions are meant to be permanent and unchangeable, so a mismatch means something wrote to the table directly and that write needs finding.

E-PUB-004.user_message: You don't have access to this map.
E-PUB-004.what_happened: Someone asked for a map's readiness or published versions while not being its owner.
E-PUB-004.likely_cause: A stale link or bookmark pointing at someone else's map, or a bug passing the wrong map id.
E-PUB-004.fix_hint: Check the Health page timeline for this Reference to see which map and user were involved. If it keeps happening for a real user, a screen is loading an id it shouldn't have.

E-PUB-005.user_message: This map is archived and can't be published.
E-PUB-005.what_happened: Publish was refused because the map's status is archived.
E-PUB-005.likely_cause: The map was archived earlier, and a page left open still shows its Publish button.
E-PUB-005.fix_hint: Un-archive the map first if it should still be in use. Nothing was published.

E-SCHED-001.user_message: That work is already on the schedule.
E-SCHED-001.what_happened: A step, or a card covering several steps, was sent for scheduling when it already holds a slot. BLK-1 made the wording depend on which: one step, or a whole card of them.
E-SCHED-001.likely_cause: The backlog was open in two places, or the step was scheduled a moment ago from another screen.
E-SCHED-001.fix_hint: Reload the backlog — a step that is already scheduled disappears from it. Each step gets one slot, so the same work can never be given out twice.

E-SCHED-002.user_message: Enter a duration between 1 and 1,440 minutes.
E-SCHED-002.what_happened: A scheduled duration was saved as zero, negative, fractional, or longer than a day.
E-SCHED-002.likely_cause: The field was cleared, or hours were typed where minutes were expected.
E-SCHED-002.fix_hint: Durations are whole minutes, so two hours is 120. Something longer than a day should be split across days. Your typing was kept.

E-SCHED-003.user_message: Someone else changed this. Reload to see the latest.
E-SCHED-003.what_happened: A duration was saved against a value that had already moved on — someone else edited the same slot first.
E-SCHED-003.likely_cause: Two people planning the same day at once, or the same plan open in two tabs.
E-SCHED-003.fix_hint: Reload and make the change again. Nothing was lost: the refused save was never written, and the other person's change is intact.

E-SCHED-005.user_message: Pick a reason from the list or choose 'Other'.
E-SCHED-005.what_happened: A duration was changed with a reason that is not one of the job's own details.
E-SCHED-005.likely_cause: The detail the reason referred to was renamed or removed after the form was opened.
E-SCHED-005.fix_hint: Reasons point at one of the job's recorded details so the change can be explained later. If none fits, choose Other. Giving no reason at all is also fine.

E-SCHED-006.user_message: That day is already live, so this step can't be taken off it.
E-SCHED-006.what_happened: A job step was unscheduled from a day that has already been published.
E-SCHED-006.likely_cause: The day was published after the step was placed on it, and the planner changed their mind afterwards.
E-SCHED-006.fix_hint: Publishing freezes a day and hands it to the person doing the work, so its contents can't be pulled back out. Nothing is lost: the step is still there, and the performer can skip it with a reason if it shouldn't be done.

E-SCHED-007.user_message: Work has already been recorded on this step, so it can't be unscheduled.
E-SCHED-007.what_happened: A job step was unscheduled after it had been started, finished, blocked, skipped, or had a note left on it.
E-SCHED-007.likely_cause: Someone began the work between the step being scheduled and the planner changing their mind.
E-SCHED-007.fix_hint: Removing the slot would orphan what was already recorded against it. The step can still be moved to a different day, and the person doing it can skip it with a reason.

E-SCHED-008.user_message: That job is cancelled, so its steps can't be scheduled.
E-SCHED-008.what_happened: A step from a cancelled job was scheduled onto a day.
E-SCHED-008.likely_cause: The job was cancelled while the backlog was open.
E-SCHED-008.fix_hint: Reload the backlog — a cancelled job’s steps drop out of it. Its history stays, but it is no longer work waiting to happen.

E-SCHED-009.user_message: Enter the start time as two digits each, like 09:00.
E-SCHED-009.what_happened: A step's start time was set by hand, but the time wasn't a valid 24-hour HH:MM (00:00 to 23:59).
E-SCHED-009.likely_cause: A typo, or a time typed with am/pm instead of 24-hour.
E-SCHED-009.fix_hint: Type the time as HH:MM, 24-hour — 14:30, not 2:30pm. Nothing was saved, so the step keeps its old start.

E-SCHED-010.user_message: Put this on someone's day first — a step in Unscheduled has no start time to change.
E-SCHED-010.what_happened: A start time was set on a step that is still in Unscheduled (not on any day).
E-SCHED-010.likely_cause: The step was moved back to Unscheduled while its edit window was open.
E-SCHED-010.fix_hint: Drag the step onto a day (or use Place…), then set its start. A start time only means something on a day.

E-SCHED-011.user_message: Keep the reason to 200 characters or fewer.
E-SCHED-011.what_happened: A start time was set by hand with a reason longer than 200 characters.
E-SCHED-011.likely_cause: A long note was pasted into the reason.
E-SCHED-011.fix_hint: Shorten the reason. Longer context belongs in the step's notes.

E-STAGE-001.user_message: Pick an owner from this map's rows.
E-STAGE-001.what_happened: A stage was saved with an owner that is not one of the rows on that map.
E-STAGE-001.likely_cause: The owner picker was showing a row from a different map, usually because the page was left open while the map changed.
E-STAGE-001.fix_hint: Reload the map and pick the owner again. If the right row genuinely isn't in the list, add it to the map first.

E-TIME-001.user_message: Enter how long this takes as a number, like 15.
E-TIME-001.what_happened: A duration value was missing, negative, or not a number.
E-TIME-001.likely_cause: The field was left as text, or a negative number was typed.
E-TIME-001.fix_hint: Enter a number of 0 or more.

E-TIME-002.user_message: Pick a unit: minutes, hours, days or weeks.
E-TIME-002.what_happened: A duration unit was missing or not one of the four allowed units.
E-TIME-002.likely_cause: The unit picker was left unset, or a direct API call sent an unexpected value.
E-TIME-002.fix_hint: Choose one of the listed units.

E-TIME-003.user_message: Add both a number and a unit, or leave both empty.
E-TIME-003.what_happened: Only one of the duration value and unit was filled in.
E-TIME-003.likely_cause: A number was typed without picking a unit, or a unit was picked without a number.
E-TIME-003.fix_hint: Fill in both fields, or clear both to leave the duration unset.

E-VAL-001.what_happened: A required field was left empty or contained only whitespace.
E-VAL-001.likely_cause: The field was skipped, or only spaces were typed into it.
E-VAL-001.fix_hint: Fill in the field and try again. Your other entries were kept.
E-VAL-001.message_varies_why: Generic "required" code: the sentence names the field.

E-VAL-002.what_happened: A value was longer than the field allows.
E-VAL-002.likely_cause: Pasted text, or a very long sentence where a short label was expected.
E-VAL-002.fix_hint: Shorten the value to the field's limit.
E-VAL-002.message_varies_why: Generic "too long" code: the sentence names the field and its limit.

E-VAL-003.what_happened: A number, date or time was not in a valid format, or a number was outside its allowed range.
E-VAL-003.likely_cause: A typo, or a value copied from somewhere with a different format.
E-VAL-003.fix_hint: Check the expected format or range and try again.

E-VAL-004.user_message: That isn't one of the allowed options.
E-VAL-004.what_happened: A value was outside the fixed list this field accepts.
E-VAL-004.likely_cause: A direct API call, or stale choices in an old browser tab.
E-VAL-004.fix_hint: Pick one of the listed options and try again.
E-VAL-004.message_varies_why: Generic "not an allowed value" code: the sentence names the rule.

E-VAL-005.user_message: That can't contain formatting like that.
E-VAL-005.what_happened: A value looked like it contained an HTML tag, which this field does not allow.
E-VAL-005.likely_cause: Text copied from a web page or rich-text editor brought formatting codes with it.
E-VAL-005.fix_hint: Paste as plain text, or remove the angle-bracket formatting.

E-VAL-006.what_happened: A name that must be unique already exists.
E-VAL-006.likely_cause: Someone already created something with this name (matching is case- and space-insensitive).
E-VAL-006.fix_hint: Pick a different name, or find and use the existing one.

E-VAL-007.what_happened: A reference pointed at something that doesn't exist, is archived, or belongs to a different account.
E-VAL-007.likely_cause: A stale link, or something that was archived or deleted after this screen loaded.
E-VAL-007.fix_hint: Reload and try again. If it keeps happening, the Health page timeline for this Reference will show which entity was involved.
E-VAL-007.message_varies_why: Generic "not found" code: the sentence names the thing.

E-ORD-004.user_message: That actor type is not one I know, so no row was created.
E-ORD-004.what_happened: A row was requested with an actor_type that is not one of the eight the app defines.
E-ORD-004.likely_cause: The AI invented an actor type. The matrix wizard can only offer valid ones, so this is almost always an AI call, not a person.
E-ORD-004.fix_hint: The message lists the eight valid types. Nothing was created; ask again naming one of them.

E-ORD-005.user_message: This column (or row) can't be removed because tasks in a published plan still point at it.
E-ORD-005.what_happened: A remove was refused because work_task rows in a published version of this map are pinned to the column's or row's key.
E-ORD-005.likely_cause: The map has been published and put to work. A work_task's identity is (work_item_id, stage_key, lens_key), so deleting the key would strand live execution records.
E-ORD-005.fix_hint: Finish or remove that work first, or rename the column instead — a rename keeps the key, which is what execution records point at.

E-BLK-001.user_message: That card has no steps waiting to be scheduled. Refresh and try again.
E-BLK-001.what_happened: A card was sent for scheduling but the server found no unscheduled steps for that job and actor row.
E-BLK-001.likely_cause: The screen is stale: somebody else scheduled it, or the job's steps moved, after the page loaded. Refetch, don't retry.
E-BLK-001.fix_hint: Reload the backlog. Nothing was scheduled and nothing was changed.

E-USR-001.user_message: Only an account admin can do that.
E-USR-001.what_happened: A user whose role is 'member' called an admin-only team endpoint.
E-USR-001.likely_cause: The caller is not an admin of their account, or the UI control was reached directly by URL or by calling the API.
E-USR-001.fix_hint: If this person should be able to manage the team, an existing admin can change their role on the Team page.

E-USR-002.user_message: We couldn't find that person in your account.
E-USR-002.what_happened: A team change named a user who is not in the caller's account, or does not exist.
E-USR-002.likely_cause: A stale Team page, or a request built by hand with another account's user id.
E-USR-002.fix_hint: Reload the Team page. This code is deliberately the same whether the user is missing or simply belongs elsewhere, so a refusal never confirms that an id exists.

E-USR-003.user_message: That would leave your account with no admin. Make someone else an admin first.
E-USR-003.what_happened: A role change or deactivation would have dropped the account's count of active admins to zero.
E-USR-003.likely_cause: The only admin tried to step down or switch themselves off.
E-USR-003.fix_hint: Promote another active member to admin, then retry. Deactivated admins do not count.

E-USR-004.user_message: You can't change your own role or switch yourself off.
E-USR-004.what_happened: A user targeted their own record with a role change or a deactivation.
E-USR-004.likely_cause: Expected: this is a guard rail, not a fault.
E-USR-004.fix_hint: Ask another admin to make the change.

E-USR-005.user_message: This account has been switched off. Ask your admin to turn it back on.
E-USR-005.what_happened: A deactivated user tried to sign in, or made a request with a token issued before they were deactivated.
E-USR-005.likely_cause: An admin deactivated them on the Team page.
E-USR-005.fix_hint: An admin can reactivate them on the Team page; their role and work are preserved.

E-USR-006.user_message: You don't have access to this part of the product. Ask your admin to turn it on.
E-USR-006.what_happened: A signed-in user called an endpoint in a module they have not been granted. The permission middleware refused the request before the endpoint ran.
E-USR-006.likely_cause: Nobody has ticked that module for them on the Team page. A new user starts with all three switched off.
E-USR-006.fix_hint: An admin can grant Intelligent Layer, Planner or Execution per person on the Team page. This code is about the caller's own access; E-USR-017 is the same refusal aimed at somebody else.

E-USR-007.what_happened: A grant or a permission check named a module key that is not one of intelligence, planning or execution.
E-USR-007.likely_cause: A request built by hand, a stale client, or a typo in a module key. The allow-list lives in one function (usr/module_keys) and nothing is written without passing it.
E-USR-007.fix_hint: Use one of intelligence, planning or execution. A fourth module means editing usr/module_keys and the MODULES list in team/teamModel.ts together.

E-USR-008.user_message: That email address is already in use.
E-USR-008.what_happened: Adding a person used an email that already belongs to a user record.
E-USR-008.likely_cause: The person already has an account, possibly in a different account than the caller's.
E-USR-008.fix_hint: Check the team list first. An email can belong to only one user across the whole product.

E-USR-009.user_message: That isn't a role we recognise. Choose admin or member.
E-USR-009.what_happened: A role change named something other than 'admin' or 'member'.
E-USR-009.likely_cause: A request built by hand. The UI only ever offers the two valid roles.
E-USR-009.fix_hint: The role column is an enum of exactly 'admin' and 'member'. Adding a third role is a schema change, not a new string.

E-USR-010.user_message: We couldn't find your user record.
E-USR-010.what_happened: An authenticated request resolved to a user id with no matching row in the user table.
E-USR-010.likely_cause: The user was removed directly in the database while still holding a valid token.
E-USR-010.fix_hint: A user row can only be removed by admin/user_delete, which refuses anyone who still has work in the system. A token belonging to a removed user keeps failing until somebody signs in again, which is correct.

E-USR-011.user_message: A name and an email address are both needed.
E-USR-011.what_happened: Adding or correcting a person arrived with no name, or no email address, or neither.
E-USR-011.likely_cause: A blank field on the Add form, or an update that sent nothing to change.
E-USR-011.fix_hint: Both are required columns on the user table. An omitted optional text input arrives as an empty string rather than null, so the server tests for empty explicitly: a blank field and a missing field are the same refusal.

E-USR-012.user_message: A password needs at least 8 characters, including a letter and a number.
E-USR-012.what_happened: An admin set an initial password that the user table's own validators would have rejected.
E-USR-012.likely_cause: A short password, or one with no digit in it, typed on the Add form.
E-USR-012.fix_hint: These are the same three rules the password column enforces. The endpoint checks them first so the admin gets this sentence instead of a raw database error.

E-USR-013.user_message: That person has work in the system, so removing them would break its history. Switch them off instead.
E-USR-013.what_happened: A delete was refused because the user id is still referenced by an architecture they own, a planner agent, an agent profile, or a performed step.
E-USR-013.likely_cause: Expected: this is the guard rail that makes a hard delete safe to offer at all.
E-USR-013.fix_hint: Switching someone off keeps every reference intact and is reversible. Deleting is for rows that are genuinely safe to destroy: a wrong address, a test account, someone who never signed in. event_log is deliberately not counted, because a historical entry naming a removed person is what an audit trail is for.

E-USR-014.user_message: That doesn't look like an email address.
E-USR-014.what_happened: A new person, or a name and email correction, carried an address that failed the shape check.
E-USR-014.likely_cause: A typo: a missing at-sign, a missing dot, or a space inside the address.
E-USR-014.fix_hint: The check is deliberately loose (something@something.something). It exists to catch a typo before it becomes a person who can never sign in, not to adjudicate RFC 5322.

E-USR-015.user_message: You can't remove your own account. Ask another admin to do it.
E-USR-015.what_happened: An admin aimed the delete endpoint at their own user id.
E-USR-015.likely_cause: Expected: this is a guard rail, not a fault.
E-USR-015.fix_hint: Separate from E-USR-004 on purpose, because removal is a different action with a different remedy: a role change or a deactivation can be undone by any admin, and a removal cannot be undone by anybody. An admin who deleted themselves would also be holding a token for a user row that no longer exists.

E-USR-020.user_message: You can't change your own access. Ask another admin.
E-USR-020.what_happened: An admin tried to grant or revoke a module on their own record.
E-USR-020.likely_cause: Expected: this is a guard rail, not a fault. It stops the only admin revoking their own Intelligent Layer access, after which nobody could reach the maps and nobody could grant it back.
E-USR-020.fix_hint: Ask another admin to make the change. The rule applies in both directions on purpose, so it reads the same whichever way the switch moved. E-USR-004 is the same guard rail for a role change or a deactivation.

E-CAT-001.user_message: Use a short id with letters, numbers and hyphens, like chair-resin.
E-CAT-001.what_happened: An item type or method key was saved with fewer than 2 or more than 40 characters, or with a character other than a lowercase letter, digit or hyphen, or starting with a hyphen.
E-CAT-001.likely_cause: The key was typed by hand instead of using the suggested one, or included spaces or punctuation.
E-CAT-001.fix_hint: The key is what rates and orders reference later, so keep it short and plain. Edit the suggested key rather than typing a new one from scratch.

E-CAT-002.user_message: You already have an item with that id.
E-CAT-002.what_happened: An item type was created with a key that another item type in this account already uses.
E-CAT-002.likely_cause: The same item was added twice, often under a slightly different label.
E-CAT-002.fix_hint: Find the existing item in the list and edit it instead of creating a second one.

E-CAT-003.user_message: Give it a name up to 80 characters, with no HTML.
E-CAT-003.what_happened: An item type or method label was saved empty, over 80 characters, or containing an HTML tag.
E-CAT-003.likely_cause: The name field was left blank, or text was pasted in from somewhere that included formatting tags.
E-CAT-003.fix_hint: Paste as plain text and keep the name to a sentence or less.

E-CAT-004.user_message: Pick a unit: each, set or pair.
E-CAT-004.what_happened: An item type's unit was left blank or set to something other than each, set or pair.
E-CAT-004.likely_cause: The unit dropdown was left at its empty default, or a value outside the three choices was sent.
E-CAT-004.fix_hint: Most items are 'each'. Use 'set' when one line should cover a whole group of pieces, like a game.

E-CAT-005.user_message: This is used by a map or a published version. Deactivate it instead.
E-CAT-005.what_happened: A delete was refused because the item type or method is already referenced by a map's item list or a published version's rate card.
E-CAT-005.likely_cause: The item or method has already been put to use, so removing it would orphan whatever points at it.
E-CAT-005.fix_hint: Deactivate it from the catalog list instead. It disappears from new maps but published versions and history keep working.

E-CAT-006.user_message: You can't change another account's catalog.
E-CAT-006.what_happened: A create, update, deactivate or delete was attempted against an item type or method that belongs to a different account.
E-CAT-006.likely_cause: A stale id, or a request built outside the normal screen.
E-CAT-006.fix_hint: Reload the catalog screen and use the item or method from your own account's list.

E-CAT-007.user_message: Pick a map from your own account.
E-CAT-007.what_happened: A method's sub-journey map was set to a map id that does not exist, or belongs to a different account.
E-CAT-007.likely_cause: A stale map list, or an id from somewhere else.
E-CAT-007.fix_hint: Reload the map picker. Only maps this account owns can be a method's sub-journey.

E-CAT-008.user_message: You already have a method with that id.
E-CAT-008.what_happened: A method was created with a key that another method in this account already uses.
E-CAT-008.likely_cause: The same method was added twice, often under a slightly different label.
E-CAT-008.fix_hint: Find the existing method in the list and edit it instead of creating a second one.

E-CAT-009.user_message: Keep the size label short, up to 20 characters.
E-CAT-009.what_happened: An item type's size label was saved with more than 20 characters.
E-CAT-009.likely_cause: A full description was typed where a short grouping label like '6ft' or 'large' was expected.
E-CAT-009.fix_hint: The size label is only used to group and report on items — it never affects any calculation, so keep it brief.

E-CAT-010.user_message: Keep the external reference up to 60 characters, with no HTML.
E-CAT-010.what_happened: An item type's external reference (the booking or inventory SKU) was saved over 60 characters or containing an HTML tag.
E-CAT-010.likely_cause: Something other than a plain SKU or code was pasted into the field.
E-CAT-010.fix_hint: Paste the SKU or code only, as plain text.

E-CAT-011.user_message: Pick an active method from your own account, or leave it blank.
E-CAT-011.what_happened: An item type's default method was set to a method id that does not exist, belongs to a different account, or has been deactivated.
E-CAT-011.likely_cause: A stale method list, a deactivated method, or an id from somewhere else.
E-CAT-011.fix_hint: Reload the method list. The default method only seeds a suggestion when this item is first used on a map — it can always be overridden there.

E-CAT-012.user_message: Only an account admin can deactivate, reactivate or delete a catalog entry.
E-CAT-012.what_happened: A non-admin tried to change an item type or method's active status, or delete one.
E-CAT-012.likely_cause: Any account member can create an item type or method, but turning one off, back on, or removing it needs an admin.
E-CAT-012.fix_hint: Ask an account admin to make the change, or edit a field other than the active status yourself.

E-ITM-001.user_message: This map already has an Items row.
E-ITM-001.what_happened: A second Items row was requested for a map that already has one.
E-ITM-001.likely_cause: The Add Items Row button was clicked twice, or two tabs tried to create it at once.
E-ITM-001.fix_hint: Reload the map — the existing Items row is already there, at the bottom.

E-ITM-002.user_message: Add that item to this map's item list first.
E-ITM-002.what_happened: An Items cell line, or the map's chosen-item list itself, referenced an item that is inactive, belongs to a different account, or was never added to this map's item list.
E-ITM-002.likely_cause: The item picker is out of date, or an item was deactivated in the catalog after this map chose it.
E-ITM-002.fix_hint: Open Choose items on the Items row and add it, or pick an item already in the list.

E-ITM-003.user_message: Choose per order, per unit or per flagged unit.
E-ITM-003.what_happened: An Items cell was saved with a scaling choice other than the three allowed values.
E-ITM-003.likely_cause: A stale form state, or a direct API call with a typo in the value.
E-ITM-003.fix_hint: Reopen the cell editor and pick one of the three options.

E-ITM-004.user_message: Enter minutes for one item, like 2.5, or leave it empty for now.
E-ITM-004.what_happened: A line's minutes-per-unit was negative, over 1440 (a full day), or had more than 2 decimal places.
E-ITM-004.likely_cause: A typo, or pasting a value that wasn't really a minutes figure.
E-ITM-004.fix_hint: Enter a number between 0 and 1440 with at most 2 decimal places, or leave the box empty.

E-ITM-005.user_message: Pick a method from your catalog.
E-ITM-005.what_happened: A line named a method that is inactive, belongs to a different account, or does not exist.
E-ITM-005.likely_cause: The method list is out of date, or a method was deactivated after a cell line was already using it.
E-ITM-005.fix_hint: Reload the method list and pick an active one.

E-ITM-006.user_message: That item already has a line for that method here.
E-ITM-006.what_happened: An Items cell was saved with two lines naming the same item and the same method.
E-ITM-006.likely_cause: The add-a-line control was used twice for the same item/method pair instead of editing the existing line.
E-ITM-006.fix_hint: Remove the duplicate line, or pick a different method for the second one.

E-ITM-007.user_message: The Items row can't own a stage — pick a person or team row.
E-ITM-007.what_happened: A stage's owner was set to the Items row, which is a perspective (what's in the job), not an actor that can be accountable for a stage.
E-ITM-007.likely_cause: The owner picker listed every row, including the Items row, without filtering it out.
E-ITM-007.fix_hint: Pick an actual actor row as the owner. If the Items row shows up in an owner picker, that picker needs to exclude template_key = items-v1.

E-ITM-008.user_message: The Items row doesn't do planned work; that switch stays off.
E-ITM-008.what_happened: Something tried to turn on "does planned work" for the Items row, which never performs planned work by design.
E-ITM-008.likely_cause: The planned-work toggle was shown for the Items row when it should have been hidden.
E-ITM-008.fix_hint: The Items row should never show a planned-work toggle. If it does, that control needs to exclude template_key = items-v1.

E-RATE-001.user_message: An item on this map was deactivated. Remove its line or reactivate it, then publish.
E-RATE-001.what_happened: Publish was refused because a rate on this map uses an item that has been deactivated in the catalog. A new version may not pin a rate for a dead item; older versions keep theirs.
E-RATE-001.likely_cause: The item was deactivated in the catalog after its line was added to the Items row.
E-RATE-001.fix_hint: Open the map's Items row, remove that item's line from every stage (or reactivate the item in the catalog), then publish again.

E-RATE-002.user_message: This map has published rates. Set every stage to per order and publish again instead of removing the row.
E-RATE-002.what_happened: Removing the Items row was refused because at least one published version of this map carries rates.
E-RATE-002.likely_cause: Someone tried to delete the Items row after the map was published with rates.
E-RATE-002.fix_hint: Set every stage's Items cell to per order, then publish a new version. The old versions keep their rates, which is the honest history.

E-RATE-003.user_message: A published version is missing rate rows.
E-RATE-003.what_happened: The nightly audit found a version whose stage_rate rows do not match the rates frozen in its snapshot.
E-RATE-003.likely_cause: A stage_rate row was deleted or added outside the publish path (a direct database edit or a restore gone wrong).
E-RATE-003.fix_hint: Run ops/audit_rates to see which version. Re-materialize the missing rows from that version's snapshot.rates; never edit the snapshot itself.

E-ITM-009.user_message: The Items row is removed with its own Remove row button.
E-ITM-009.what_happened: A generic row-delete path (journey/remove_lens: the matrix's row delete or an AI tool) was asked to delete the Items row, which would skip its own cleanup and the published-rates guard.
E-ITM-009.likely_cause: A screen or AI tool offered the generic row delete on the Items row.
E-ITM-009.fix_hint: Delete the Items row with its Remove row button (endpoint 603). If a screen or AI tool offered the generic delete on the Items row, that control needs to exclude template_key = items-v1.

E-ITM-010.user_message: Edit an Items cell with the Items cell editor.
E-ITM-010.what_happened: The generic cell update (endpoint 44) was asked to write an Items cell's item lines, which would skip validate_items_cell and link reconciliation.
E-ITM-010.likely_cause: A screen or tool saved an Items cell through the generic cell editor instead of the Items cell editor.
E-ITM-010.fix_hint: Save Items cells through the Items cell editor (endpoint 605). Status and lock changes through the generic update are still allowed.

E-EST-001.what_happened: An order line's quantity was outside 1-9999 or not a whole number.
E-EST-001.likely_cause: A typo, or an empty quantity box.
E-EST-001.fix_hint: Enter a whole number from 1 to 9999.

E-EST-002.user_message: That item has been deactivated. Pick another or reactivate it in Settings → Items.
E-EST-002.what_happened: An order line named an item that has been deactivated in the catalog.
E-EST-002.likely_cause: The item was deactivated after this order was started, or the picker is out of date.
E-EST-002.fix_hint: Reactivate the item in Settings → Items, or pick a different one for this line.

E-EST-003.user_message: That item isn't on this map. Add it to the map's Items row and publish a new version.
E-EST-003.what_happened: An order line named an item that the job's published version has no rate for on any stage — it was never part of this map's Items row, or belongs to a different account.
E-EST-003.likely_cause: The item picker is out of date, or the item was never added to this map's Items row.
E-EST-003.fix_hint: Open the map's Items row, add the item with a rate, publish a new version, then create a new order.

E-EST-004.user_message: This work type doesn't track items. Add an Items row to the map and publish a new version.
E-EST-004.what_happened: Order lines were submitted for a job whose map has no Items row at all.
E-EST-004.likely_cause: The map was never set up to track item counts.
E-EST-004.fix_hint: Add an Items row to the map, give it rates, publish a new version, then create a new order against it.

E-EST-005.user_message: This job isn't linked to a published version yet.
E-EST-005.what_happened: A job's order lines were requested, but the job has no pinned published version.
E-EST-005.likely_cause: A data problem — every job should be pinned to a version at creation.
E-EST-005.fix_hint: Check how this job was created; it should always be pinned to a published version.

E-EST-006.user_message: That item is already on this order — change its quantity instead.
E-EST-006.what_happened: The same item appeared twice in one order-lines update.
E-EST-006.likely_cause: The add-item control was used twice for the same item instead of editing its existing line.
E-EST-006.fix_hint: Remove the duplicate line and update the quantity on the one that's left.

E-EST-007.user_message: Work has started on this order, so its items are locked. Create a new order for the extra items.
E-EST-007.what_happened: An order's lines were edited after at least one of its steps had already started.
E-EST-007.likely_cause: Someone tried to change what's in an order that's already being worked.
E-EST-007.fix_hint: Create a new order for any additional items — this order's estimate must not drift under live work.

E-EXC-001.user_message: That job is finished or cancelled, so nothing can be sent from it or added under it.
E-EXC-001.what_happened: Someone tried to send part of a job to a linked map from a job that was already completed or cancelled, or to add a new job under a cancelled parent.
E-EXC-001.likely_cause: The job was closed between loading the screen and pressing Send, or the parent picked for a new job is cancelled.
E-EXC-001.fix_hint: Reload the job. If the work really needs to go somewhere, add a new job for it.

E-EXC-002.user_message: This step doesn't send work to that map. Add an exception link on the map and publish a new version — new jobs will have it.
E-EXC-002.what_happened: A send-to request named a map that the job's pinned version does not link to as an exception at this step's stage, or a map in another account.
E-EXC-002.likely_cause: The exception link was added to the live map after this job started (jobs keep the version they started with), or the request was built by hand.
E-EXC-002.fix_hint: Add the exception link on the map, publish a new version, and use it on jobs created after that. This job cannot gain the link.

E-EXC-003.user_message: That map hasn't been published yet. Publish it, then try again.
E-EXC-003.what_happened: A send-to request pointed at a linked map that has no published version, so there is nothing to pin the new job to.
E-EXC-003.likely_cause: The linked map was created but never published. Readiness warned about this on the parent map (exception_map_unpublished).
E-EXC-003.fix_hint: Open the linked map, publish a version, then send the work again.

E-EXC-004.user_message: This work type doesn't track items, so you can't pick which ones to send. Send the whole step instead.
E-EXC-004.what_happened: Item counts were sent with a send-to request on a job whose map has no Items row.
E-EXC-004.likely_cause: The request included counts for a job that has none.
E-EXC-004.fix_hint: Send without counts. To track items, add an Items row to the map and publish a new version.

E-EXC-005.user_message: That item isn't on this order.
E-EXC-005.what_happened: A send-to request listed an item that is not one of the job's order lines.
E-EXC-005.likely_cause: The order changed since the screen was loaded, or the request was built by hand.
E-EXC-005.fix_hint: Reload the job and pick from the items shown.

E-EXC-006.user_message: Enter how many to send, from 1 up to how many are on the order.
E-EXC-006.what_happened: A send-to request asked to move zero, a negative or fractional number, or more than the order holds of an item.
E-EXC-006.likely_cause: A typing mistake, or the order's count went down since the screen was loaded.
E-EXC-006.fix_hint: Enter a whole number between 1 and the count on the order.

E-EXC-007.user_message: That item is listed twice — combine them.
E-EXC-007.what_happened: The same item appeared twice in one send-to request.
E-EXC-007.likely_cause: The item was added twice instead of raising its count.
E-EXC-007.fix_hint: Remove the duplicate and put the full count on one line.

E-EXC-008.user_message: The linked map doesn't track items, so the counts can't go with the work. Add an Items row to it and publish, or send without counts.
E-EXC-008.what_happened: Counts were sent to a linked map whose latest published version has no Items row, so the new job could not hold them.
E-EXC-008.likely_cause: The linked map was built without an Items row.
E-EXC-008.fix_hint: Either send the step without counts, or add an Items row to the linked map, publish it, and try again.

E-EXC-009.user_message: That parent job is in a different plan.
E-EXC-009.what_happened: A job was added with a parent job that does not exist, is in another account, or is in a different plan.
E-EXC-009.likely_cause: The parent id was copied from another plan, or the request was built by hand.
E-EXC-009.fix_hint: Pick a parent job from the same plan.

E-EXC-010.what_happened: A send-to request had no reason, or one that is not on the fixed list (waiting on someone, missing information, something went wrong, other).
E-EXC-010.likely_cause: The reason was left empty, or an old app version sent an unknown value.
E-EXC-010.fix_hint: Choose one of the four reasons and send again.

E-EXC-011.user_message: Keep the note under 500 characters, with no HTML.
E-EXC-011.what_happened: A send-to request's note was longer than 500 characters or contained HTML.
E-EXC-011.likely_cause: A long paste, or copied formatting.
E-EXC-011.fix_hint: Shorten the note, or remove any formatting, and send again.

E-EXC-012.user_message: The order changed while you were sending. Close this and try again.
E-EXC-012.what_happened: Another send (or an order edit) changed this job's lines between the checks and the save, so nothing was written.
E-EXC-012.likely_cause: Two people sent items from the same job at the same moment.
E-EXC-012.fix_hint: Reopen the job to see its current counts, then send again.

E-EXC-013.user_message: This was already sent. Reopen the job to see it.
E-EXC-013.what_happened: A send-to request repeated one that had already saved (same request), so no second child job was made.
E-EXC-013.likely_cause: The first response was lost (a slow phone connection) and Send was tapped again. The app treats this as sent.
E-EXC-013.fix_hint: Nothing to do: the first send made the child job. Reopen the job to see it.

E-EXC-014.user_message: We couldn't open that job just now. Try again.
E-EXC-014.what_happened: The job view failed to load the other job's steps.
E-EXC-014.likely_cause: A dropped connection or a server error.
E-EXC-014.fix_hint: Try again. If it keeps happening, quote the Reference to support.

E-EXC-015.user_message: That job isn't available any more.
E-EXC-015.what_happened: The job view asked for a job that no longer exists in this account.
E-EXC-015.likely_cause: The job belongs to another account, or the link is stale.
E-EXC-015.fix_hint: Nothing to fix on the job you're on. Ask a planner if the sent work was moved.

E-TW-001.user_message: Enter a start and end date, and times as two digits each, like 09:00.
E-TW-001.what_happened: A time window was saved with a missing date, or a time that isn't between 00:00 and 23:59.
E-TW-001.likely_cause: A field was left empty, or a time was typed as 9:5 or 25:00.
E-TW-001.fix_hint: Use the 24-hour clock with two digits each: 09:00, 17:30. Your typing was kept.

E-TW-002.user_message: The window has to end after it starts.
E-TW-002.what_happened: A time window's end was the same as, or earlier than, its start.
E-TW-002.likely_cause: The end time was typed before the start time, or the end date was left on an earlier day.
E-TW-002.fix_hint: A window can run past midnight — set the end date to the next day for overnight work.

E-TW-003.user_message: This time window falls completely outside the plan's dates.
E-TW-003.what_happened: A time window was saved that doesn't overlap the plan's window at all.
E-TW-003.likely_cause: The wrong month or year was picked, or the job belongs in a different plan.
E-TW-003.fix_hint: The full message names the plan's dates. At least part of the time window must sit inside them.

E-TW-004.user_message: That job isn't available any more.
E-TW-004.what_happened: A time window was read or changed for a job that doesn't exist in this account.
E-TW-004.likely_cause: The job belongs to another account, or the page is out of date.
E-TW-004.fix_hint: Reload the plan. If the job is still listed, quote the Reference to support.

E-TW-005.user_message: This job is cancelled, so its time window can't be changed.
E-TW-005.what_happened: A time window was set or removed on a cancelled job.
E-TW-005.likely_cause: The job was cancelled after the page was opened.
E-TW-005.fix_hint: A cancelled job keeps its window as history. Add a new job if the work is still needed.

E-TW-006.user_message: Keep the time window's note to 200 characters or fewer.
E-TW-006.what_happened: A time window was saved with a note longer than 200 characters.
E-TW-006.likely_cause: A long explanation or pasted text went into the note.
E-TW-006.fix_hint: The note is a short reason, like "site opens at 9". Put longer detail on the job itself. Your typing was kept.

E-SEC-020.user_message: Sign in to use these tools.
E-SEC-020.what_happened: An outside assistant connected to the AI tool address without a valid token, or with a token whose owner is switched off or lacks the Intelligent Layer. The gate returned no tools, so nothing could be listed or run.
E-SEC-020.likely_cause: The connection has no token, the token expired, or the person behind it has not been granted the Intelligent Layer.
E-SEC-020.fix_hint: Create a token (automation_api_token/generate) and add it to the assistant's connection as a Bearer header, or as ?token= on the address. If the token is valid, check the person is switched on and has the Intelligent Layer on the Team page. Add a valid Emgram token to the connection.

E-COP-001.user_message: You don't have access to this part of the product. Ask your admin to turn it on.
E-COP-001.what_happened: An AI tool was called by a person (directly, or through an agent working for them) who is switched off or has not been granted the Intelligent Layer. The tool gate refused the call before the tool ran.
E-COP-001.likely_cause: The person's Intelligent Layer access was never ticked on the Team page, or they were switched off after they started a chat or connected an assistant.
E-COP-001.fix_hint: An admin can grant the Intelligent Layer, or switch the person back on, on the Team page. Every refusal is also in tool_call_log with verdict 'refused'.

E-COP-002.what_happened: An AI tool named a map or business that is not in the caller's account, or does not exist. The answer is deliberately the same for both, so a caller cannot learn which ids are real.
E-COP-002.likely_cause: The AI was asked about a map from another account, or was given an id that is wrong or deleted.
E-COP-002.fix_hint: Check the id belongs to the account the person signed in with. A refusal for a business says 'Journey Architecture not found' under the same code.

E-COP-004.user_message: The copilot has reached today's limit and is paused until tomorrow.
E-COP-004.what_happened: The account's copilot (an AI identity) made as many AI tool calls today (UTC) as its daily limit allows. The gate refused the call before the tool ran. One 'cap reached' event is written per copilot per day.
E-COP-004.likely_cause: The limit is low for the work asked of it, or something is calling tools in a loop.
E-COP-004.fix_hint: An account admin can raise the limit (admin/copilot_cap). Check tool_call_log for that user today to see what used the calls.

E-COP-006.user_message: This account already has a copilot. Switch it off or rename it instead.
E-COP-006.what_happened: An admin tried to create a second copilot. The database refused it (one copilot per account is a unique index), so nothing was saved.
E-COP-006.likely_cause: Someone clicked create twice, or did not know the account already has one.
E-COP-006.fix_hint: Use the existing copilot; GET account/copilot shows it.

E-COP-007.user_message: We could not create the copilot. Nothing was saved.
E-COP-007.what_happened: Creating the copilot's user row, its ai_identity row or its Intelligent Layer grant failed inside one transaction, so all three were rolled back. The underlying message is appended.
E-COP-007.likely_cause: A database rule refused one of the rows for a reason other than 'already has one'.
E-COP-007.fix_hint: Read the appended message; if it names a validator, the account or user data may be unusual. Safe to retry.

E-COP-008.user_message: This account does not have a copilot yet.
E-COP-008.what_happened: A copilot action was asked for in an account that has no copilot, or by a user who is not in an account.
E-COP-008.likely_cause: The copilot has not been created for this account.
E-COP-008.fix_hint: An account admin can create one (admin/copilot_create).

E-COP-009.user_message: The daily limit must be a whole number from 0 to 100000.
E-COP-009.what_happened: An admin sent a daily limit outside the allowed range. Nothing was changed.
E-COP-009.likely_cause: A typo, or a negative number.

E-COP-010.user_message: Your user is not in an account yet, so it cannot have a copilot.
E-COP-010.what_happened: An admin with no account (account_id 0) tried to create a copilot. Nothing was saved.
E-COP-010.likely_cause: An old sign-up from before accounts existed (see Epic-22 F-8).
E-COP-010.fix_hint: Put the user in an account first; then create the copilot.

E-COP-011.user_message: The copilot can't be removed, because it is the record of everything the AI did. Switch it off instead.
E-COP-011.what_happened: An admin tried to delete the user row that is the account's copilot. Removing it would leave the AI audit trail and the maps it made pointing at nobody, so the delete was refused before anything changed.
E-COP-011.likely_cause: The copilot looked like any other person on Manage users.
E-COP-011.fix_hint: Switch the copilot off on Manage users; its next tool call is then refused.

E-COP-012.user_message: The copilot's email address can't be changed — it is what stops anyone signing in as the copilot. You can still rename it.
E-COP-012.what_happened: An admin tried to change the copilot's email. Its .invalid address can never receive a reset or magic link, which is what keeps every copilot action inside the tool gate (daily limit and audit trail). The change was refused before anything was written.
E-COP-012.likely_cause: The copilot looked like any other person on Manage users.
E-COP-012.fix_hint: Rename the copilot if needed; leave its address alone.

E-COP-013.user_message: The copilot's role can't be changed. What it can do is set by its module access.
